To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deep learning techniques can increase the performance of BLSTM neural networks by a large margin.

deep BLSTM networks outperform shallow BLSTM networks for unconstrained handwritten text recognition, that the number of hidden layers has a strong influence on the performance, but that the type of hidden layer (rectified linear or hyperbolic tangent) does not.

(1) deep learning approaches outperform BLSTM NNs for unconstrained handwriting recognition; (2) the type of hidden layers used in the deep learning approach has a significant influence on the performance; (3) the performance of deep learning approaches can further be improved by using BLSTM NNs as a feature extraction method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how deep learning techniques can be used to improve the recognition performance for the task of handwriting recognition.
the following questions: 1) What is the effect of the depth of the network? 2) How does the depth interact with the width of the network (number of neurons per layer)?
the following questions: (1) How does the number of layers and the number of neurons affect the recognition performance of deep BLSTMs?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
deep BLSTMs are superior to shallow BLSTMs and shallow BLSTMs are better than BLSTMs.
the best results are achieved when combining deep learning and bidirectional recurrent neural networks.
a deep BLSTM neural network architecture outperforms a shallow BLSTM neural network by 2.1% in terms of word accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
deep learning approaches are a promising way to improve the recognition accuracy of handwriting recognition systems.
we can achieve the best recognition accuracy on the IAM database with a deep BLSTM network, which consists of 4 BLSTM layers and 2 hidden layers in between, trained with a dropout technique.
we can improve the recognition performance of BLSTM neural networks by using deeper networks with more hidden layers and by using a combination of hidden layer types.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of deep learning techniques can be beneficial for the task of handwriting recognition.
the performance of BLSTMs is significantly improved when using a large number of hidden layers, which is in contrast to what is commonly observed for other tasks.
deep BLSTM neural networks are a promising approach to improve recognition accuracy in unconstrained handwritten text recognition.
